first_impression.reaction: My fiancee wants five bridesmaids flown overseas and I want to know what that means before anyone books, so I Googled it. The opening line is a bit warm and fuzzy, but the second sentence gives a plain definition, so I stayed. Went to the FAQ first as usual, then straight to the destination section because that's where the money and the arguments are. Skimmed the history for dates.

journey.quote: No one has to. Ask early, talk openly about who covers travel and time off, and make it easy for a friend to decline and still come as a guest.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, no guilt trip. That's the line I'd show my fiancee.

journey.quote: Queen Victoria had twelve bridesmaids in 1840, all eldest daughters of peers, dressed in white to her own design.
journey.reaction: A year, a number, a detail I can check against the Royal Collection link further down. Fine.

journey.section: 3. Queen Victoria's bridesmaids and royal attendants
journey.quote: A long train or cathedral veil needs one or two named attendants, briefed and rehearsed on the actual aisle, steps and turns of your ceremony venue.
journey.reaction: Good, the history actually turns into something practical instead of just trivia.

journey.quote: Who covers flights and accommodation, and is that the same for every attendant?
journey.reaction: This is the exact question that causes the fight. Glad it's spelt out, and the 'same for every attendant' bit is the trap people miss.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises getting travel insurance whoever you are and wherever you are going, and treats the right policy as essential as a passport.
journey.reaction: Dated and pointed at the government site, not a sponsored insurer. Nobody's trying to sell me a policy. Good.

journey.quote: Each attendant checks their own passport is valid for at least six months beyond the end of the trip, and their own visa for every country they visit or transit through.
journey.reaction: Concrete and puts responsibility in the right place. The transit point is useful.

journey.quote: When you are ready to plan the trip around the people you love, speak with a Wedded Advisor.
journey.reaction: 'The people you love' is a bit of a greeting card. At least it comes after the useful stuff, and the next sentence about inclusions in writing is what I actually care about.

journey.section: 7. What bridesmaids and the maid of honour do, before and on the day
journey.quote: Victoria's Duchess of Sutherland did much the same.
journey.reaction: Slightly forced link back to the Queen in the middle of a to-do list. Doesn't hurt, doesn't help.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me how the fee is worked out or whether you take a cut from the venue or hotel on top.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues, hotels or suppliers on top of the advisor fee?
What does the Wedded Advisor fee cover and how is it calculated?
Is the first conversation with a Wedded Advisor free, and what does it cover?
Can the advisor handle bookings for attendants paying their own way, or only the couple's bookings?

turn_offs_found.quote: When you are ready to plan the trip around the people you love, speak with a Wedded Advisor.
turn_offs_found.why: Mild emotional phrasing on the sales line. It's not an unsupported claim and it sits after the evidence, so it's minor, but a plainer line would land better with me.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the FAQ answer on whether bridesmaids have to travel and the 'questions to talk through together' list
The bridal party group chat, for the passport, visa and insurance points before anyone books

cta_reaction.quote: You will work with one Wedded Advisor, your single point of contact from the first conversation to the wedding day.
cta_reaction.why: CTAs come after the useful content and the fee-in-writing line is what I look for. Nothing here put me off. But a post about bridesmaids won't make me enquire on its own; I'd want to see how you charge and whether suppliers pay you first.

top_3_changes: Nice-to-have: make the mid-article CTA plainer, e.g. drop 'around the people you love' and lead with what the advisor actually does.
Nice-to-have (business detail deferred): say in one line whether the Wedded Advisor takes commissions or mark-ups from suppliers.
Nothing else would stop me enquiring; no must-fix changes from me.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft (link text quoted as rendered)
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for dates, catches, who pays, fee model, commissions
No invented brand facts; missing fee, commission and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Every turn-off has a why; journey types limited to the allowed set
Title and deferred business details not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing lines; no price requests

open_questions.question: Is a fees or how-we-charge page available to link from the closing CTA? Business details are deferred, so treat as nice-to-have.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'why do we have bridesmaids' because his fiancee is planning to fly her bridesmaids overseas; relevance is moderate because of the destination section, not the history.
No prices on the page is the house standard for this article and not penalised.
